$comment: The single source for first-run install instructions. Two surfaces render this and they
must not drift: the download page (apps/coil-home/src/lib/install.ts, which shows the steps
inline with copy buttons) and every GitHub release body (scripts/coil/render-release-notes.mjs,
which the release workflow writes to a file and passes as the release notes).
Before this file existed the only copy lived inline in .github/workflows/coil-release.yml, and
the download page merely said the release notes 'carry the commands to get past it' without
linking them — so a user could go from the landing page to a broken app having never seen a
appBundleName is a CACHED COPY of apps/desktop/package.json's productName, which is what
resolveDesktopProductName). It is duplicated here because neither renderer should have to
reach into the desktop app's package.json at render time — and render-release-notes.test.ts
asserts the two agree, so the rename in #71 turns this from silent drift into a failing test.

platforms.name: macOS
platforms.support: Apple Silicon (arm64) only. There is no Intel build.

steps.title: Drag the app to /Applications before you launch it
steps.body: Do this first, from the mounted disk image. Launching it from the image instead triggers macOS App Translocation, which runs the app from a randomised read-only path — and the in-app updater then refuses to replace it. Nothing tells you this has happened; updates just stop working.

steps.title: Remove the quarantine flag
steps.body: Without this macOS says the app **is damaged and should be moved to the Trash**, not that it is from an unidentified developer — and right-click → Open does **not** get past that wording. The app is not damaged: it carries Electron's inherited ad-hoc signature with no sealed resources, and this is what that looks like from the outside.

platforms.afterword: In-app updates strip quarantine themselves, so this is a first-install step only — you should not need it again.

platforms.name: Windows
platforms.support: x64 only, Windows 10 and 11. There is no arm64 build.

steps.title: Clear the Mark of the Web on the installer
steps.body: Run this in the folder you downloaded it to. Windows tags files from the internet, and SmartScreen reads that tag.

steps.title: Choose More info → Run anyway at the SmartScreen prompt
steps.body: SmartScreen still warns, because the installer is unsigned. The **Run anyway** button is behind the **More info** link — it is not shown until you click that.

platforms.afterword: Later updates install themselves, so this is a first-install step only.

unsignedNote: These builds are not code-signed or notarized, which is why both platforms need a step here. Linux is not built at all — build from source instead.
